rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil says the passage was revealed about al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil after Khabbāb made jewelry for him and asked for his fee.
rows.anchor: نزلت في العاص بن وائل بن هشام بن سعد بن سعيد بن عمرو بن هصيص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about God's signs means the verses of the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: { أفرأيت الذي كفر بآياتنا } ، آيات القرآن

rows.speaker: العاص
rows.claim: Al-ʿĀṣ mocked Khabbāb by saying he would receive better wealth and children in Paradise and repay him there.
rows.anchor: قال العاص: فميعاد ما بيننا الجنة، { وقال لأوتين } في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿĀṣ spoke mockingly because he did not believe the Qur’an’s promises of reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: يقول ذلك مستهزئا؛ لأنه لا يؤمن بما في القرآن من الثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether al-ʿĀṣ had knowledge of the unseen when he claimed he would receive believers’ afterlife rewards.
rows.anchor: يعني العاص، حين يقول: إنه يعطى في الآخرة ما يعطى المؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having a covenant with the Merciful means believing in divine oneness.
rows.anchor: أم اعتقد عند الرحمن التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No indeed” denies that al-ʿĀṣ will receive what believers receive.
rows.anchor: لا يعطي العاص ما يعطي المؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recording is done by the guardian angels, who write down al-ʿĀṣ’s claim about receiving the believers’ reward.
rows.anchor: من الحفظة من الملائكة تكتب ما يقول العاص أن يعطى ما يعطى المؤمنون في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment extended for al-ʿĀṣ has no end.
rows.anchor: يعني الذى لا نقطاع له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inherits from al-ʿĀṣ the reward he claimed and gives it to someone else.
rows.anchor: فنرثه عنه ويعطاه غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿĀṣ will come to God in the afterlife alone, with nothing from his worldly life.
rows.anchor: العاص في الآخرة، ليس معه شىء من دنياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage refers to Meccan unbelievers including al-ʿĀṣ, al-Naḍr, and Abū Jahl.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر كفار مكة: العاص، والنضر، وأبا جهل، وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their adopted deities are al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, Manāt, and Hubal.
rows.anchor: يعني اللات، والعزى، ومناة، وهبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They took the idols as protection to keep God from harming them; Yā Sīn 36:74 uses the same sense of preventing.
rows.anchor: يعني منعا يمنعونهم من الله عز وجل، نظيرها في يس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No indeed” means the idols cannot protect their worshippers from God.
rows.anchor: لا تمنعهم الآلهة من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the afterlife the idols will disown everyone who worshipped them in this world.
rows.anchor: ستبرأ الآلهة في الآخرة من كل من كان يعبدها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols will become their worshippers’ enemies; in the parallels cited, “ʿalā” carries the sense “for,” as in Qur’an 2:143 and 5:3.
rows.anchor: تكون آلهتهم يومئذ لهم أعداء، كقوله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The targeted unbelievers are Quraysh’s mockers; the sending of devils recalls God’s command to Iblīs in 17:64 to entice people by his call.
rows.anchor: يعني المستهزئين من قريش حين قال سبحانه إبليس، وهو الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devils agitate and incite them, beautify their shirk, and tell them their course is right.
rows.anchor: يعني تزعجهم إزعاجا، وتغريهم إغراء، تزين لهم الذى هم عليه من الشرك، ويقول: إن الأمر الذى أنتم عليه لأمر حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells the Prophet not to hasten the unbelievers’ punishment.
rows.anchor: يقول للنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم: فلا تستعجل لهم بالعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is counting their lifespans and their breaths before punishment comes upon them.
rows.anchor: { إنما نعد لهم } آجالهم، { عدا } [آية: 84]، يعني الأنفاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pious are those who avoid shirk, meaning the monotheists.
rows.anchor: الشرك، يعني الموحدين، { إلى الرحمن وفدا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They come as a delegation mounted on noble camels, with saddles likened to the platforms of city-dwellers.
rows.anchor: على النجائب على رحلاتها منابر الحضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals are driven to Hell thirsty, seeing it as they enter.
rows.anchor: يرونها في الدخول وهم عطاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels cannot intercede for anyone.
rows.anchor: لا تقدر الملائكة على الشافعة لأحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception to intercession is one who believes in divine oneness and affirms the testimony that none is deity but God alone.
rows.anchor: يعني إلا من اعتقد التوحيد عند الرحمن جل جلاله، وهى شهادة ألا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that God took a child means they said the angels were God's daughters; al-Naḍr b. al-Ḥārith was among them.
rows.anchor: من الملائكة، حين قالوا: إنهن بنات الله تعالى، منهم: النضر بن الحارث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling angels daughters of the Merciful is a tremendous statement, like the accusation in Qur’an 17:40.
rows.anchor: قلتم قولا عظيما، نظيرها في بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens nearly split, the earth splits at its edges, and the mountains collapse because of their slander that angels are daughters of the Merciful; these mighty things are named to show its enormity.
rows.anchor: يعني مما قالوا: إن الملائكة بنات الرحمن، { وتنشق الأرض } من أطرافها، { وتخر الجبال هدا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The charge is that people said the Merciful had a child.
rows.anchor: أن قالوا: للرحمن ولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is unfitting for the Merciful to take a child.
rows.anchor: وما ينبغي للرحمن أن يتخذ ولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All in the heavens and earth, including angels, ʿUzayr, Jesus, Mary, and others, come to the Merciful as servants who acknowledge servitude to him.
rows.anchor: من الملائكة وغيرهم، وعزير، وعيسى، ومريم وغيرهم، فهؤلاء في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has recorded all their names in the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: أحصى أسماءهم في اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the number of all of them.
rows.anchor: يقول سبحانه: علم عددهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone will come on the Day of Resurrection alone, with nothing from worldly life.
rows.anchor: يعني وحده ليس معه من دنياه شىء
